verified.analysis: The triage note conflates two things. The Fifth Circuit appeal is genuinely live but is NOT dated — the Georgetown litigation tracker shows briefing complete (opening 2026-02-13, response 2026-03-27, reply 2026-04-17, Clover supplemental authority 2026-06-02) with no oral argument or decision date set, so it cannot anchor a dated-binary position. What IS dated and forward is the CMS 2027 Star Ratings release in early October 2026, where Humana has publicly committed to beating its 20% 4+ star membership share; that clears G1/G2 and has not fired. The disqualifier is re-rating: HUM has nearly tripled off the $163 low to $400 near 52-week highs, so the favorable outcome is already discounted and the residual payoff is skewed negative — keep it on the board as a dated risk marker rather than an ACTIVE entry, and revisit only on a meaningful drawdown into September.

verified.bloom_gates: G2 (FDA-accepted NDA with an assigned, company-confirmed action date, plus a committed EMA filing by YE2026); G1 partial (FDA/EMA are named counterparties but regulatory review is not a commercial commitment); G3 fails - no specific currently-unpriced figure identified
verified.edge: L - the value-creating event (Ph3 RINGSIDE efficacy) already printed and the stock has re-rated from an $8.67 52wk low to ~$22 / $2.1B cap; the PDUFA is a high-probability confirmatory step, not an information event
verified.primary_source: Immunome press release via Businesswire/StockTitan, "Immunome Announces U.S. FDA Acceptance of NDA for Varegacestat," 08-Jul-2026; price/cap from FMP quote 20-Jul-2026
verified.analysis: Verified: FDA accepted the varegacestat NDA on 08-Jul-2026 with a PDUFA target action date of 28-Apr-2027 (standard review), backed by Ph3 RINGSIDE showing an 84% reduction in progression/death risk (HR ~0.16) and 56% vs 9% ORR in 156 randomized patients; an EMA MAA is committed by end-2026. The catalyst is real, dated and forward, but the asymmetry is muted on three counts: the efficacy uncertainty is already resolved, the date is ~9 months out with no intervening value event, and varegacestat would be the second gamma-secretase inhibitor to market behind SpringWorks' Ogsiveo (approved 2023), so the debate is commercial share rather than approval risk. At a $2.1B cap trading near 52-week highs after a ~2.6x run, approval looks substantially discounted; the residual edge would be a negative surprise (CRL/label restriction) rather than upside, which is the wrong shape for a long catalyst position.
